branch: impoverished camera protocols as headline ceiling-below-1 numbers, plus the four-view phantom rate needed for the fifth-camera claim
what: Recomputes R1 (ideal-extraction ceiling) under two-view and three-view camera subsets on the frozen five-camera geometry, at both the certified tolerance (tau=0.01) and the released ray-tolerance (0.15), as first-class headline quantities rather than a census footnote. Also computes the four-view (and five-view) phantom-nonempty rate at near-zero tolerance to settle whether the fifth camera does real work.
protocol: frozen five-camera set (axis_a, axis_b, axis_c, body_diagonal, oblique2); ideal-extraction oracle (reconstruct_positions + recover_symmetry, render_ceiling.reconstruct), symprec=0.01, angle_tolerance=5.0
fifth_camera_claim_verdict: The fifth-camera claim survives only in the fidelity/guarantee sense, not in the accuracy sense. Mean R1 accuracy saturates at four views (0.9371-1.0 depending on tolerance) and gains only 0.15-2.9 points moving to five views. But the phantom-nonempty rate drops to EXACTLY ZERO only at four views and stays zero at five (0.0% at four views on both the 210- and 1950-structure samples, at tau approx 0), matching the earlier three-view rate of 1.9% which is still nonzero. The fifth camera's marginal, measurable contribution is therefore the elimination of the LAST residual phantom-producing failure mode down to a certified-empty guarantee, not an accuracy gain and not the two/three-view rates the manuscript currently cites in the same sentence (those describe the second and third camera's contribution).
provenance: recomputed independently via scripts/run_ceiling_sweep_n210.py, scripts/run_phantom_census_e3.py, scripts/run_phantom_census_e50.py; reproduces results/view_subset_sweep/summary.json's tol=0.15 numbers (0.7481/0.9152/0.9371/0.9524) exactly, and results/option_a_frontier/results.json's ck_2_3_phantoms1933 two/three-view rates (0.1542/0.0187) exactly.
